message.content:
Finding the “best” sushi spot in Los Angeles is a bit of a moving target—taste, service, price point, and even the vibe you’re after all play a role. Below is a quick snapshot of the most frequently cited top‑tier sushi restaurants in LA (as of 2024), grouped by what they’re known for. Feel free to pick the one that matches your mood or budget!

| Restaurant | Why It’s Notable | Typical Price Range | Atmosphere & Tips |
|------------|-----------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| **Sushi Gen** (Koreatown) | 2 Michelin stars; legendary for its omakase and fresh, high‑quality fish. | $200–$300 per person (omakase) | Intimate, no‑frills counter service. Book months ahead. |
| **Sushi Zo** (West Hollywood) | 1 Michelin star; known for its creative rolls and meticulous presentation. | $150–$250 per person (omakase) | Sleek, modern interior; great for a special night out. |
| **Sushi Ota** (Beverly Hills) | 1 Michelin star; famed for its “Ota Roll” and a menu that balances tradition with innovation. | $120–$200 per person (omakase) | Classic Japanese décor; reservations recommended. |
| **Sushi Park** (West Hollywood) | 1 Michelin star; praised for its seasonal ingredients and a relaxed yet refined setting. | $120–$180 per person (omakase) | Cozy, counter‑style dining; often has a “chef’s choice” option. |
| **Sushi Tetsu** (Hollywood) | 1 Michelin star; celebrated for its “sushi bar” experience and a menu that changes daily. | $100–$170 per person (omakase) | Minimalist, counter‑only; perfect for sushi purists. |
| **Sushi Katsu** (Beverly Hills) | 1 Michelin star; known for its “Katsu Roll” and a focus on sustainable sourcing. | $110–$160 per person (omakase) | Elegant, quiet setting; great for business lunches. |
| **Sushi Nori** (West Hollywood) | 1 Michelin star; offers a “Chef’s Table” experience with a rotating menu. | $140–$220 per person (omakase) | Intimate, chef‑centric; requires advance booking. |
| **Sushi Saito** (Beverly Hills) | 1 Michelin star; a hidden gem with a focus on traditional Edomae techniques. | $130–$210 per person (omakase) | Very small, counter‑only; reservations months in advance. |
| **Sushi Tatsu** (West Hollywood) | 1 Michelin star; known for its “Tatsu Roll” and a menu that blends classic and contemporary. | $120–$190 per person (omakase) | Modern, sleek décor; great for a date night. |
| **Sushi Maki** (Beverly Hills) | 1 Michelin star; praised for its “Maki Roll” and a menu that highlights seasonal fish. | $110–$170 per person (omakase) | Classic Japanese décor; reservations recommended. |

### How to Choose

| Factor | What to Look For |
|--------|------------------|
| **Budget** | Omakase at Michelin‑starred spots can run $200–$300+. If you’re looking for something more affordable, consider places like **Sushi Gen**’s “Chef’s Choice” or **Sushi Park**’s “Chef’s Table” options. |
| **Vibe** | Counter‑only, intimate settings (e.g., **Sushi Tetsu**, **Sushi Saito**) are great for a focused sushi experience. If you want a more lively atmosphere, **Sushi Zo** or **Sushi Ota** offer a modern, upscale vibe. |
| **Special Occasion** | For a truly memorable night, book a Michelin‑starred omakase. Many of these restaurants require reservations months in advance. |
| **Seasonal Menus** | Restaurants that change their menu daily (like **Sushi Tetsu** or **Sushi Park**) ensure you get the freshest fish available. |
| **Location** | All listed spots are in West Hollywood, Beverly Hills, or Koreatown—easy to reach from most parts of LA. |

### Quick Booking Tips

1. **Reserve Early** – Michelin‑starred spots fill up fast; aim for at least 2–3 months in advance.
2. **Ask About Chef’s Specials** – Some restaurants offer a “Chef’s Choice” omakase that’s slightly cheaper but still top quality.
3. **Check for Seasonal Menus** – If you’re flexible, ask if the chef has a special seasonal tasting menu; it can be a unique experience.

---

#### Bottom Line

If you’re after the pinnacle of sushi in LA, **Sushi Gen** and **Sushi Zo** are the clear front‑runners, each boasting Michelin stars and a reputation for impeccable quality. For a slightly less pricey yet still stellar experience, **Sushi Park** and **Sushi Ota** are excellent choices. Whichever you pick, you’ll be treated to some of the finest sushi the city has to offer. Enjoy!
